analysis.detail: Log4Shell. Remediated in release 1.1.0 by upgrading log4j-core from 2.14.1 to 2.17.1 under CR-4821. The finding was Affected in 1.0.0 and CISA KEV-listed with known ransomware use; this statement is retained as the remediation record for the 510(k) submission.
Closed by the same 2.17.1 upgrade. Assessed Not Affected in 1.0.0 on configuration grounds (no ${ctx:} lookup pattern); the upgrade removes the reliance on that configuration control.

Command injection in lodash.template. Fixed upstream in 4.17.21, which this release ships; the scanner matched on an advisory range that includes the patched version. Additionally the production bundle is tree-shaken to lodash.get and lodash.merge, so template is absent from the shipped artifact.

ReDoS in the axios trim helper, reachable from telemetry upload header parsing. Carried over unremediated from release 1.0.0 — axios remains at 0.21.1 because the 1.x upgrade changes the interceptor contract used by the retry layer. Owner: platform-security. Planned for release 1.2.0 under CR-4890; compensating control is the 8 KB header cap at the ingress proxy.

Open redirect via res.location in express 4.17.1, newly introduced by this release. Assessing whether any redirect target derives from request input on the clinician callback route. Owner: platform-security. Target date: 2026-09-30.

XSS via res.redirect in express. The telemetry service exposes only JSON API routes and never calls res.redirect; the sole redirect in the codebase is a static constant in the health probe. Verified by grep over the 1.1.0 source tree and by route inventory review.
